eligibility_text: You must be a veteran enrolled in VA health care, and the appointment must be at a VA health facility or a VA-authorized community care provider (source wording). Call to confirm.
phone: 804-675-5000, then select 0 and ask for a VTP representative
how_to_apply: Call 804-675-5000, select 0 and ask for a Veterans Transportation Program representative. Or request a ride online with VetRide (you need an ID.me or Login.gov account). The deadline to ask for a ride depends on the facility.
source_notes: Read from va.gov on 2026-11-05. The phone number is from the VA Richmond healthcare entry on the main source. Eligibility, VetRide and the deadline note are from the additional source. VA lists the Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center under VA Richmond health care. The main source also lists a Beneficiary Travel Office (mileage pay) at 804-675-5000, ext. 4006. No counties are listed, so service area is left empty.

eligibility_text: For veterans and their families, per the source. Age requirement: 18 and over. Call to confirm.
address: 10300 Spotsylvania Avenue, Lee Hill Building 1, Suite 290, Fredericksburg, VA 22408
hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. Veterans are seen 8:30 am to 3:00 pm by appointment only. Closed to the public on the last business day of the month.
how_to_apply: Call 540-376-7298 for an appointment, or schedule one online. Veterans are seen by appointment only.
source_notes: Read from the source page on 2026-11-05. The source also lists Northumberland and Westmoreland counties, which are outside this app's area. It does not list Stafford County. Website is the source's "Visit Program" link.
name: Virginia Department of Veterans Services, Fredericksburg office
description: State office where a service representative can help a veteran and family learn what local, state and federal benefits are available. All services are free.

eligibility_text: Not stated by source. The source says help from an accredited VSO representative on VA claims is always free, but accredited attorneys and claims agents can charge fees.
how_to_apply: Use VA's search tool to find a representative and ask if they can help. Then you both sign VA Form 21-22 (for a VSO) or 21-22a (for an attorney or claims agent) and submit it online, by mail or at a VA regional office.
source_notes: Read from va.gov on 2026-11-05. National service, shown here as available statewide. For in-person help nearby, see the Virginia Department of Veterans Services office listing.
name: Get help from a VA-accredited representative or VSO
description: An accredited Veterans Service Organization (VSO) representative, attorney or claims agent can help you file a VA claim or ask for a decision review. VA has an online tool to find one.

how_to_apply: Call 800-827-1000. For TTY, dial 711.

name: VA benefits hotline
description: Phone line for questions about VA benefits, such as the status of a disability, pension or survivors claim or appeal, requesting a letter, or updating your address or direct deposit.

name: Virginia Veterans Navigator

eligibility_text: For service members and veterans with a service-connected disability that limits or prevents their ability to work (source wording). Check eligibility on the source.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the source page. It also links an eligibility check and how-to-apply steps.
source_notes: Read from va.gov on 2026-11-05. National service, shown here as available statewide. The source lists no phone number.
name: Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E, Chapter 31)
description: Job and training help for service members and veterans with a service-connected disability. Options include finding a new job, returning to a former job, starting a business, education counseling and help living independently.

eligibility_text: Outpatient care for veterans in the Northern Virginia and Central Virginia area, per the source. This page does not explain VA health care enrollment. Call to confirm.
hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Saturday and Sunday closed. Hours vary by service.
how_to_apply: Call 540-707-7074 to schedule, change or cancel an appointment. The source says primary care does not need a referral. You can also call VA Health Connect at 855-679-0074.
source_notes: Read from va.gov on 2026-11-05. The page title is "Fredericksburg 3 VA Clinic"; the page text calls it the Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center. The source says it serves veterans in the Northern and Central Virginia area but lists no counties, so service area is left empty.
name: Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center
description: VA outpatient care center with primary care, pharmacy, lab tests, hearing and vision care, pain care, chiropractic care and more. Part of the Central Virginia VA Health Care System.

eligibility_text: For veterans and service members, per the source. VA decides who is eligible. Call to confirm.
hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. ET (phone)
how_to_apply: Apply online, call 877-222-8387, mail VA Form 10-10EZ, or bring a signed form to the nearest VA medical center or clinic. Have your discharge papers, insurance information and last year's household income ready.
source_notes: Read from va.gov on 2026-11-05. National service, shown here as available statewide. The source says a decision usually takes less than 1 week.
name: Apply for VA health care
description: Apply to get health care through VA online, by phone, by mail or in person. An accredited representative or Veterans Service Organization can help you apply.

eligibility_text: Depends on your VA dental benefits class, for example a service-connected dental condition, former prisoner of war status, or a 100% disability rating (source summary). VADIP insurance requires VA health care or CHAMPVA. Call to confirm.
how_to_apply: Apply for VA health care first. If you are already enrolled, you don't need to reapply; find a VA dental clinic near you.
source_notes: Read from va.gov on 2026-11-05. National service, shown here as available statewide. The source lists no phone number.
name: VA dental care
description: Some veterans can get some or all of their dental care through VA, depending on service history, health and living situation. Veterans who can't may be able to buy lower-cost dental insurance through VA (VADIP).

eligibility_text: For veterans. The source says some veterans may be able to get mental health care without enrolling in VA health care, and that this service needs a referral. Call to confirm.
hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
how_to_apply: Call 540-707-7153. The source says you can visit with or without an appointment, but this service needs a referral, so you may need to contact your VA primary care provider first.
source_notes: Read from the Mental health care section of the va.gov Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center page on 2026-11-05. The source lists no counties, so service area is left empty.
name: Mental health care, Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center
description: Counseling and treatment for PTSD, depression, anxiety, grief, anger, trauma, addiction and more, with individual and group therapy. The source says all VA health care facilities offer same-day help.

eligibility_text: For veterans in crisis and people concerned about a veteran, per the source.
how_to_apply: Call 988 and select 1, text 838255, or start a confidential chat online. For TTY, call 711 then 988.
source_notes: Read from va.gov on 2026-11-05. veteranscrisisline.net could not be reached from the build environment, so the website field is the chat link the va.gov page gives. These are the numbers the crisis footer shows on every page.
name: Veterans Crisis Line
description: Free, private help for veterans in crisis, any time, day or night. Many responders are veterans. Call 988 and select 1, text 838255, or chat online.

eligibility_text: Veterans who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless due to financial hardship, unemployment, addiction, depression, or transition from jail (source wording). Call to confirm.
how_to_apply: If you are homeless or within 14 days of becoming homeless, call 804-675-5000, ext. 12041 to talk with an intake specialist.
source_notes: Read from va.gov on 2026-11-05. Phone, eligibility and services are from the main source. The Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center page (additional source) says homeless veteran care is also offered there, with or without an appointment. Neither page lists the counties served.

name: Health Care for Homeless Veterans
organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA Richmond health care)
description: Help for veterans who are homeless or about to be. Care coordinators can help with food and shelter, transitional and permanent housing, job training, money to prevent homelessness, addiction and depression treatment, and health and dental care.

eligibility_text: Veterans who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless. Family, friends or neighbors can also call; the source says they don't need to know the veteran's military details or confirm eligibility first.
how_to_apply: Call 877-424-3838 any time, or chat online. A counselor will ask about your situation and connect you to help.
source_notes: Read from va.gov on 2026-11-05. National service, shown here as available statewide. "Free" is from the VA contact page (additional source).

name: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans
description: Free, private calls with a trained VA counselor for veterans who are homeless or at risk. They can help with safe shelter, short-term money to prevent homelessness, talking with landlords and long-term housing, and connect you to local help.

eligibility_text: For caregivers of veterans, per the source. The Fredericksburg VA page says caregivers of veterans injured after 9/11 may be eligible for more services, such as a stipend, training and medical coverage. Call to confirm.
how_to_apply: Call a VA Richmond caregiver support coordinator at 804-675-6631. For questions about caregiver services nationwide, or if you need someone to listen right now, call the VA Caregiver Support Line at 855-260-3274.
source_notes: Read from va.gov on 2026-11-05. The note about post-9/11 caregivers is from the Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center page (additional source), which also lists caregiver support there. Neither page lists the counties served.
